report_emails.subject: Put Tally before your automation
report_emails.single_idea: Tally is now available as a form front end for automations: it can push new submissions into workflows built with Make, Zapier, or n8n, and the webhook route is free to use.
unresolved: Unresolved strategy/material gap: The email asks the reader to create a form to judge whether “the form itself is worth wiring up,” but its evidence establishes only webhook availability and transport, not why evaluating the form alone resolves this audience’s operational concern. The argument must instead make form creation the first bounded step toward testing supported webhook behavior—such as structured JSON delivery and documented failure handling—without implying that creating the form validates the integration.

reader_verdicts.what_it_sells: Tally is a form builder that can send new intake submissions into Make, Zapier, or n8n through a free webhook, potentially replacing a separate paid form front end.
reader_verdicts.relevance_feedback: The profile explicitly makes intake forms the first step of an ownerless automation, so the premise is relevant. The email additionally assumes I have a forthcoming workflow and may use Make, Zapier, or n8n; those tools and timing are plausible but not established.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: I handle an intake form that begins an automation nobody owns.
Email-only: I am preparing a next automation that needs a new form front end.
Email-only: I use or would choose Make, Zapier, or n8n.
Email-only: avoiding API polling or CSV exports is important in this workflow.
Email-only: I am ready to configure an endpoint and send a fresh test submission.
reader_verdicts.problem_now: A dependable form-to-automation handoff matters for this role, but no active build, failure, or deadline is established. Payload quality, delivery behavior, validation, and downstream mapping are plausible operational risks that the email does not address.
reader_verdicts.stopped_at: Once the webhook is connected, Tally pushes each new submission when it arrives.
reader_verdicts.biggest_doubt: I cannot tell whether the webhook sends stable, usable field values or how failures and awkward field types are handled; merely pushing each submission is not enough for an intake automation I may have to maintain.
reader_verdicts.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had shown a sample webhook payload demonstrating exactly how multi-choice and email fields arrive.
fixes: Rewrite “Once the webhook is connected, Tally pushes each new submission when it arrives.” to specify what the payload contains and link to a concrete sample payload.

Cut “Your automation can then route the data to a CRM, billing tool, internal database, or messaging app—without polling the API or exporting a CSV first.” It is generic and does not answer whether the submitted values will be usable downstream.

Rewrite “Endpoint configuration and a fresh test submission can come next.” to say what I can inspect before creating a form, such as the payload format, delivery behavior, or field mapping documentation.

original_brief.single_idea: Tally is now available as a form front end for automations: it can push new submissions into workflows built with Make, Zapier, or n8n, and the webhook route is free to use.
original_brief.felt_need: After a Tally form submits to a webhook, the respondent cannot be reliably redirected or shown a conditional response from the automation tool; the connection appears to be lost once the platform returns its own 'accepted' acknowledgement.
original_brief.status_quo: Builders are advised to use the generic Webhook trigger module instead of the native Tally app module, because the native module simplifies the payload in a way that complicates handling it downstream.
original_brief.mechanism: Once a Tally form is connected through a webhook, a new submission can trigger Make, Zapier, or n8n and continue to a CRM, billing tool, internal database, or messaging app. The submission is pushed when it arrives rather than waiting for polling or a CSV export, and webhook access is available free to all Tally users.
must_not_say: Do not claim Tally’s webhook response can redirect a respondent or display an automation-generated conditional response.
Do not claim Tally fixes field-level mapping failures, including a missing email value in Airtable.
Do not claim an instant trigger processes historical submissions or that a successfully delivered submission can be replayed.
Do not claim Tally resolves multiple-choice IDs into readable labels; P2 is unsupported.
Do not claim Tally validates typos, blank fields, or every bad CRM record before write-through.
Do not describe what endpoint-response details the delivery-history view exposes or make the CTA depend on seeing that view.
Do not imply that creating a form completes or proves the automation; an endpoint must still be configured and tested with a new submission.
Do not promise no setup, flawless delivery, or end-to-end reliability.
Do not add the full feature list, security posture, customer count, paid-plan pricing, or broad integration catalog.
Do not use the unlimited-forms-and-submissions proposition in this version; reserve it for the complete alternative argument.
original_brief.next_step_value: The reader can start the form that would sit before a Make, Zapier, or n8n workflow, while knowing the webhook route itself is available free.
original_brief.next_step_limit: Creating the form does not demonstrate webhook delivery, payload shape, field mapping, respondent redirects, historical-submission behavior, or the downstream result; those require configuring an endpoint and sending a new test submission.

audience_cards_current_projection.name: The ops or no-code person on a small team whose intake form is step one of an automation nobody owns

counterevidence_summary: Signature verification is opt-in, so an endpoint can silently accept anything if the builder never sets a secret. — The same source gives a direct workaround — always set a signing secret and verify the header — so this is a configuration default to argue about, not a capability gap for a team that already reads webhook docs. Minor condition; does not exclude this audience.

The instant-trigger module cannot be edited, and the two-scenario workaround failed for this builder; the thread ends unresolved. — Where the automation has to answer the respondent — conditional redirect after submit — the builder reports the documented workaround does not work and no resolution is reached, so a whole class of ops workflows stalls. Review before prioritising.
reasons: An independent webhook-infrastructure guide states the job this audience is hiring the form for — reacting to submissions in real time instead of polling — and documents the exact delivery semantics the candidate claims they evaluate on (10-second acknowledgement, the retry ladder, HMAC-SHA256 signature, free on all plans).
A no-code automation community thread shows a real builder wiring a Tally form into Make and hitting the edge of what the webhook can do, which is buyer-adjacent behaviour in a named venue.
Both Hookdeck guides and the Make community are in the candidate's `where` list and both produced matching material, so findability is verified.
The required capability `rest_api` is verified in the supplied ledger (E31: submissions as structured JSON to any HTTP endpoint).
unknowns: No corpus evidence of who pays or how the tool is chosen inside a 5-50 person team; the buying role is still inferred.
The corpus does not state whether a delivery log with manual retry is a product feature or something the third-party gateway supplies.
No uptime, rate-limit or duplicate-delivery guarantees appear anywhere in the corpus; the guide's advice to use responseId as an idempotency key implies consumers must handle repeats.
Whether per-seat pricing sensitivity actually drives this choice is untested in the corpus.
Review the counterevidence before prioritising this audience.

evidence.claim: An independent infrastructure vendor frames the exact downstream use this segment is defined by.
evidence.quote: If you're routing form submissions into a CRM, a database, or a downstream workflow, webhooks are how you react in real time without polling.

evidence.claim: The delivery semantics this audience evaluates on are published and verifiable by a third party, including the retry ladder and the free-on-all-plans position.
evidence.quote: | Retries | 5 min, 30 min, 1 hr, 6 hr, 1 day |

evidence.claim: Signature verification is opt-in, so an endpoint can silently accept anything if the builder never sets a secret.
evidence.quote: **The Problem:** If no secret is set, deliveries are unsigned, and an endpoint that assumes a signature will either reject everything or (worse) accept anything. Any POST to an unsigned webhook URL looks legitimate.
evidence.impact_reason: The same source gives a direct workaround — always set a signing secret and verify the header — so this is a configuration default to argue about, not a capability gap for a team that already reads webhook docs.

evidence.claim: A builder in the Make community is trying to route the respondent conditionally on their answers via the webhook and cannot make it work.
evidence.quote: I have a question, from tally form I can redirect users to a link after filling out the form… Is it possible to forward to the tally trigger webhook and make a webhook response depending on their answers? help please, thanks.

evidence.claim: The instant-trigger module cannot be edited, and the two-scenario workaround failed for this builder; the thread ends unresolved.
evidence.quote: If I point the form to the tally webhook (acid instant) module, there is no way to edit this webhook.
evidence.impact_reason: Where the automation has to answer the respondent — conditional redirect after submit — the builder reports the documented workaround does not work and no resolution is reached, so a whole class of ops workflows stalls.

evidence.claim: The helper's recommended pattern requires two scenarios and a sleep, i.e. a workaround rather than a supported path.
evidence.quote: Hi! Yes, that’s generally possible but you’ll need to use two scenarios.

synthetic_final_fallback_visibility.reader_persona:
Selected audience (explicit constraints): A freelance designer or one-person studio who spends the first two weeks of every project chasing brand assets out of a client's inbox.
The context and problem reports below describe observed members of this market, not established experiences or installed tools of this recipient. The campaign request controls which job this email addresses; do not require a link to an unrequested integration in your doubts or click requirements.
Observed context (inferred; applicability must be checked): Every new engagement starts the same way: they need the logo in a usable format, the old brand guidelines PDF, photography the client owns, a rough brief, the billing details and whoever's sign-off they'll need later. None of it arrives in one place. It comes back as a reply-all thread, a file-transfer link that expires before they've downloaded it, a shared-drive invite the client's IT blocks, and a 'can you just pull it off our website?'. They almost certainly have a form somewhere already — a Google Form, a free Typeform, a page on their Squarespace site — and each one failed in its own way: the client couldn't upload without signing into an account, or the packaged InDesign file was too big for the free tier, or the form itself carried someone else's logo at the bottom, which reads badly on the one document where they are selling their own taste in branding. They are not short of tooling and they are not technical; they are short of a single link they can paste into a kickoff email and trust. If the brief is thin, the first round of work is wrong, and the rework is unbilled.

Problem context: The people who owe them files will not create an account in a tool just to hand over an attachment, so collection falls back to email (inferred); source: Collect free file uploads | Free Form Builder | Tally (https://tally.so/help/file-uploads)
Problem context: Project briefs, reference files and onboarding details arrive scattered across channels instead of in one place (inferred); source: Collect free file uploads | Free Form Builder | Tally (https://tally.so/help/file-uploads)
Problem context: The incumbent tools charge a monthly subscription before they will accept a file upload at all, which is hard to justify for a handful of kickoffs a year (inferred); source: Compare Tally: Free Form Builder vs Typeform, Jotform & More (https://tally.so/help/compare)
Problem context: Design source files and asset packs are routinely larger than the file-size ceiling on any free form tier, so the one thing they most need collected is the thing that fails (inferred); source: unknown
Problem context: A client-facing intake form that carries another company's name and favicon reads as borrowed rather than as part of the studio's own process (inferred); source: unknown
